readme: Worked examples of the intents layer. These are teaching material, NOT town canon: nobody in TestTown has actually voiced them. Each example says what it teaches and whether the validator should accept it. The tests run every one, so an example can never drift out of date. Run `python3 tools/validate_intents.py` to see them checked.

examples.title: The smallest possible intent
examples.teaches: Only three fields are required: wants, expressedAt, status. No category, no dates, no story.

examples.title: A generic intent with a start date and an expiry
examples.teaches: startDate and expiresAt are optional on a generic intent. Here the owner wants an appraisal done in January and will stop asking after February.

intent.wants: Get the mural appraised before the spring show
intent.story: The gallery asked for a current valuation ahead of the spring show.

examples.title: A category nobody has written rules for yet
examples.teaches: An unknown category is allowed. Its details block is free-form. This is how a new kind of want gets tried out before anyone writes a checker for it.

intent.wants: Lend the work van to a neighbor for a week

examples.title: The owner changed their mind
examples.teaches: withdrawn is the owner's own act. The intent stays in the dossier as history; consumers must not treat it as a live ask.

intent.story: Listed it in June, then decided to keep it in the family.

examples.title: A live insurance wish
examples.teaches: An insurance wish is a generic intent with category 'insurance'. It must have startDate, expiresAt, and an insurance block with wish and coverageUsd.

examples.title: An insurance wish that ran out unanswered
examples.teaches: expiresAt is in the past relative to frozenNow, so the status must be expired. A consumer that offers cover against this is making a mistake.

examples.title: The owner accepted an offer
examples.teaches: accepted records that the OWNER said yes to an offer. It does not say a policy was bound or that any check passed; those facts belong to the insurer's own records.

examples.title: Offer window closes before cover starts
examples.teaches: expiresAt may fall before startDate: 'my ask is open through Dec 31, for cover starting Jan 1'. This is normal renewal-season behavior, not an error.

examples.title: BROKEN: an intent that records a gate's decision
examples.teaches: The rule that must never bend. 'approved' is an outcome, and outcomes belong to gatekeepers. The validator rejects this.

examples.title: BROKEN: an insurance wish with no expiry
examples.teaches: Fine as a generic intent, but not as an insurance wish: an insurer cannot quote an ask that never goes stale.

examples.title: BROKEN: marked open after its expiry date
examples.teaches: Status and dates must agree. Past expiresAt, an unanswered intent is expired, not open.
